Summary: Love is the Bible's greatest command and its clearest picture of God: "God is love." Yet love in Scripture is not sentiment — it is patient action, costly sacrifice, and truthful commitment. This topical study follows love from 1 Corinthians 13 to 1 John, so you can learn to love the way God loves.
Steps: Read 1 Corinthians 13 slowly, substituting your own name for "love" — and notice where it convicts you; Study John 13:34-35 and 15:9-17, asking what Jesus' "new command" actually requires; Trace love through 1 John, noting how love for God and love for others prove each other; Examine one relationship where love is hard, and ask what patient, kind, truthful action looks like there; Practice one "1 Corinthians 13" quality each day for a week — patience on Monday, kindness on Tuesday, and so on; End by asking someone close to you how loved they feel by you, and listen without defending yourself
Questions: Why does Paul say love matters more than gifts, knowledge, or sacrifice — and do you agree?; What is the difference between loving someone and liking them, or approving of them?; How do you love an enemy, a difficult family member, or someone who has hurt you — practically?; Why does John say you cannot love God while hating your brother — what does that reveal about love's nature?; Where is love most costly for you right now, and what would it look like to pay that cost?
Application: Choose one person to love actively this week — not with feelings, but with a specific kind act, a patient conversation, or a forgiven debt.
